content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot, then drop sharply — suggesting overreaction to recent spikes.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections after high peaks.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing true price declines — often holds high forecasts even when recent history shows falling prices.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days of the window, then gradually adjust — suggesting a delayed response to actual trend shifts.
- Model underreacts to low-price periods in the history — fails to anticipate sharp drops when recent data shows weakening momentum.
- Overshoots after spikes, then corrects too slowly — model doesn’t fully account for momentum decay or policy-induced volatility.
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices — model doesn’t adjust downward sufficiently.
